extracted.intended_audience: open-government practitioners, federal agencies involved in rulemaking, OGP reviewers and civil society interested in notice-and-comment
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, piloting, and evaluating tools and processes (e.g., eRegulations) to make it easier for the public to find, read, compare, and comment on proposed federal regulations and to promote commenting opportunities across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment aim — enhance opportunities for public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: This commitment aimed to enhance opportunities for the public to participate in federal rulemaking by developing and piloting new ways for the public to comment on proposed regulations and promoting such commenting opportunities. The commitment aimed to expand the 'eRegulations' pilot developed by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation should include developing/piloting applications that make commenting easier and outreach to promote commenting opportunities. Success judged by whether new ways to comment were developed, piloted, and promoted across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and expansion of eRegulations (open source pilot)
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to make regulations easier to read and navigate, the Administration will expand the open source pilot developed by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to additional agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion assesses whether the eRegulations application (open-source code, GitHub-hosted) is adopted by additional agencies beyond CFPB and whether agency-specific versions converge toward shared infrastructure. Anti-pattern: agencies running disparate, non-interoperable versions; success includes cross-agency adoption and reuse of the open-source codebase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with existing platforms (Regulations.gov, APIs, FDMS)
rubrics_metrics.description: By leveraging the Regulations.gov website, application programming interfaces, and the Federal Docket Management System, the Administration will develop and pilot applications to make commenting on proposed rulemakings easier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether pilots integrate with Regulations.gov, use available APIs, and interoperate with FDMS rather than building isolated systems. Guidance: prefer reuse of established federal docket/data infrastructure to ensure discoverability and reduce duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tool features and usability (in-line definitions, compare revisions, mobile-friendly design)
rubrics_metrics.description: The eRegulations tool provides in-line interpretations and definitions, a feature for viewing and comparing revisions, and an easy-to-use design and clear typography that works on phones and tablets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors should check for presence and quality of these user-facing features: in-line interpretations/definitions, revision comparison, clear typography, responsive/mobile design. These features are cited as making it easier to access and comment on proposed regulation. Anti-pattern: clunky UI that hinders reading or commenting on specific text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granularity of commenting (paragraph-level commenting)
rubrics_metrics.description: The GSA 18F pilot project allowed users to submit comments on paragraphs of specific proposed rulemakings, as opposed to submitting comments for rulemakings as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether commenting capability supports paragraph-level or other fine-grained annotations and whether that capability was piloted, documented, and assessed. Success includes pilots that enable targeted, paragraph-level input with mechanisms to surface those comments to agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption breadth across agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: At midterm and end-of-term the eRegulations application was in use by CFPB, FEC, and ATF; most regulation remained beyond its purview and agencies ran their own versions as there was no centralized repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure success by number and diversity of federal agencies adopting the tool, movement toward centralized repository or common platform, and reduction in fragmented agency-specific versions. Limited adoption (only three agencies) is an indicator of limited progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifiability of commitment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commitments should include measurable outputs or public evidence (code on GitHub, pilot deployments, public pilot sites, reports). Here verifiable evidence includes GitHub repos, public pilot URLs, and IRM reports. Absence of publishable evaluation reduces verifiability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition level
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assesses whether the commitment aims for systemic change (e.g., expanding an open-source platform government-wide). High ambition should be matched by realistic scope, resources, and timelines; otherwise high ambition with limited follow-through signals weak implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation progress / completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation status reported as Midterm: Limited; End of term: Limited. Completion: (not specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should record stage of implementation at midterm and end-of-term and whether planned activities were executed. 'Limited' progress indicates partial or pilot-level implementation without broader rollout. Absence of stated completion date or milestones is a negative signal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early results assessment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early outcomes (user uptake, agency adoption, qualitative improvements in commenting) should be reported; 'marginal' signals limited demonstrable benefits at the time of review. Assessors should look for concrete usage metrics to move beyond 'marginal'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Did It Open Government? — Access to information
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to Information: Marginal. The tool makes it easier to access and comment on proposed regulation, but its potential is hampered by limited agency uptake and pilot status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the commitment materially improved public access to regulatory text and explanatory materials (searchability, readability, revision history). Partial improvements with limited scope or adoption justify 'marginal'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Did It Open Government? — Civic participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Civic Participation: Marginal. The tool provides features that could increase participation but with few agencies using it the effect on civic participation was limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the commitment increased the quantity and quality of public comments, lowered barriers to comment submission, and broadened participation. Limited uptake and pilot-only status reduce impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of evaluation and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The IRM researcher was unable to locate a report summarizing the pilot’s results; recommendation that 18F could release a report summarizing the paragraph-level commenting pilot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion checks for public reports or evaluations summarizing pilot findings. Absence of a public report is an implementation shortfall. Best practice: publish evaluation reports documenting user testing, adoption metrics, lessons learned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of responsible and supporting institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible Institutions: CFPB, EPA, GSA, NARA, OMB; Supporting Institutions: FEC and ATF (DOJ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commitments should clearly name lead and supporting institutions so responsibilities are clear. Assessment considers whether those institutions actively participated in implementation and whether responsibilities were coordinated across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of timelines/milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Start Date: Not Specified; End Date: Not Specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice is to include start/end dates and milestones. Lack of specified timeline hampers assessment of progress and completion; evaluators should flag missing dates as a deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized repository vs. distributed agency versions
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no centralized repository of regulation; agencies run their own versions of eRegulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether commitment moves toward a centralized, discoverable repository or leaves a fragmented landscape of agency-specific implementations. Centralization promotes discoverability and reuse; fragmentation is a weakness.
